documents: Artana et al. 2022, JGR Oceans 127, e2022JC019082, published paper (PDF, 19 pages)
pages_convention: printed journal pages (n of 19), which equal PDF pages counted from 1; Supporting Information S1 cited by name, not supplied

entry.evidence: We examined high frequency variations in the YPB using the 34 months-long data set presented in Artana et al. (2022).

sequences.source_document: Artana et al. 2022, JGR Oceans, published version

steps.action: The authors cite Padman et al. (1992)'s hypothesis that residual tidal currents (rectification or baroclinic adjustment to tidal mixing) advect Atlantic Water clockwise around the plateau, and note it has received little attention.
steps.quote: Padman et al. (1992) first hypothesized that residual tidal currents

steps.action: The authors cite prior theory and modelling: the plateau lies poleward of the critical latitude, diurnal tides generate higher harmonics (Urbancic 2022; Wang 2022), and the 2K1 harmonic can propagate freely.
steps.quote: the second harmonic (period 11.97 hr) of the diurnal tide is not subinertial over the Yermak Plateau and could freely propagate

steps.action: The authors cite the rival source of high-frequency energy: wind-forced near-inertial waves, with the hypothesis that sea-ice loss energizes the internal wave field.
steps.quote: it has been hypothetized that the massive reduction in sea ice cover would lead to a more energetic internal wave field

steps.action: The authors pose the aims: characterize tides and the contribution of residual tidal currents to low-frequency AW flow, and characterize high-frequency velocity shears across a wide range of environmental conditions.
steps.quote: The data set is complemented with numerical models to characterize tides over the Yermak Pass and investigate the contribution of residual tidal currents

steps.action: The authors reuse the 34-month mooring record (ADCP, SBE37, Aquadopp; Sept 2017 to June 2020) from their earlier study.
steps.quote: The mooring data was acquired at 80.6°N and 7.26°E, in the Yermak Pass on the eastern flank of the Yermak Plateau

steps.action: The authors check the instruments: data return near 100%, gaps interpolated, and mooring verticality from pressure (mean 355 db, std 2 db); the Appendix A pressure spectrum shows tidal-period peaks of up to 4.5 db.
steps.quote: Over the 34 months of measurements, the mooring stayed in a straight position

steps.action: The authors high-pass filter the velocities (50-hr Butterworth) and describe variance ellipses and rotary spectra: diurnal, semidiurnal and harmonic peaks, CW dominance, and over 70% of variance at high frequency.
steps.quote: High frequency variations (periods less than 50 hr) account for more than 70% of the total velocity variance.

steps.action: Using satellite sea ice, ERA5 winds, tidal model, low-pass velocity, pressure and PSY4 mixed-layer series, the authors select six winter and summer months with small ADCP vertical motion that span different conditions.
steps.quote: We selected 3 months in winter and summer with small pressure variations as study cases.

steps.action: The authors estimate tidal ellipse parameters and their uncertainties for the major constituents from ADCP and Aquadopp velocities by T_TIDE harmonic analysis; the diurnal constituents dominate.
steps.quote: We analyzed the tidal constituents present in the observed velocities using the T_TIDE Matlab toolbox

steps.action: The authors check the Arc5km2018 inverse tidal model against the observed constituents (Table 2) and rotary spectra: most constituents lie within the 95% confidence interval, but O1 and P1 are underestimated.
steps.quote: The Arc5km2018 model major constituents K1, M2, S2, N2, are close to the estimated values from observations

steps.action: The authors map Arc5km2018 tidal ellipses over the plateau and place the mooring site's relatively small tides in context, with large tides on the crest and the northern tip.
steps.quote: is rather small compared to other locations of the plateau

steps.action: The authors compare 1/36° twin simulations with and without five tidal harmonics (Jan to Mar 2013) to isolate the tidal residual mean circulation.
steps.quote: We compared mean velocities resulting from the twin simulations with a 1/36° resolution model

steps.action: The authors judge the simulated tides acceptable (not shown) and check that 1-, 2- and 3-month means and different depths give similar features.
steps.quote: Means were produced over different periods of time (1, 2, and 3 months) within the 3-month (January–March 2013) simulations and showed consistent similar features.

steps.action: The authors compare the residual field with the Padman hypothesis and rectification theory: an enhanced anticyclonic circulation around the plateau, up to 8 cm/s at the northern tip, larger where diurnal tides are strong.
steps.quote: the simulation with tides producing an enhanced anticyclonic circulation around the plateau

steps.action: The authors compare the simulated residual at the mooring (N-NE, 3 to 4 cm/s) with the independent estimate of Koenig et al. (2017) from mooring minus no-tide model velocities.
steps.quote: This direction and amplitude are consistent with residual velocities estimated in Koenig et al. (2017)

steps.action: The authors keep, as exploratory, the claim that tidal residuals matter, and infer that YPB transport from no-tide models may be overestimated.
steps.quote: this exploratory comparison suggests to further investigate residual tidal currents around the plateau and to take tides into account

steps.action: The authors compute 'baroclinic' rotary spectra and 2D wavenumber-frequency shear spectra: energy is concentrated in the CW semi-diurnal band, unlike the velocity spectra, with a dominant vertical scale of about 60 m (supplement).
steps.quote: show dominant energy in the clockwise component with energy mainly concentrated around semi-diurnal band

steps.action: The authors decompose the shear time series into stationary, upward- and downward-propagating components with the Park et al. (2004) method, for the selected low-motion cases.
steps.quote: The shear time series in the water column were decomposed into three components

steps.action: For September 2018, the authors describe the mesoscale background from PSY4 (a long-lived anticyclonic eddy) and the in situ low-frequency velocities and hydrography at the eddy's western edge.
steps.quote: According to PSY4 model, the Yermak Plateau hosted a long-lived anticyclonic eddy from March to mid-October 2018

steps.action: The authors estimate the eddy's relative vorticity (about -2e-5 s-1) from in situ swirl velocity and PSY4 radius, giving an effective inertial period near 14 hr.
steps.quote: The relative vorticity ζ associated with the eddy was tentatively estimated.

steps.action: The authors describe the September 2018 shear: it is strong at 50 to 60 m and intensifies with the eddy, and the stationary component dominates the propagating ones and has shorter length scales.
steps.quote: The stationary component amplitude is much larger than the upward and downward propagating shears

steps.action: The authors propose that modulation of the shear by the mesoscale field reflects wave trapping by the anticyclone, through a lowered effective planetary vorticity.
steps.quote: The observed modulation of the velocity shear by mesoscale activity is indicative of wave trapping by the anticyclone

steps.action: The authors note downward-propagating wave packets after strong wind bursts and downward-shear energy broadened toward 15 hr, consistent with a larger effective inertial period in eddies.
steps.quote: coherent wave packets propagate downward after September 12 and 23 when intense wind bursts occur

steps.action: The authors repeat the shear decomposition and depth-averaged spectra over all six selected months: the stationary component exceeds the propagating ones by an order of magnitude in every case.
steps.quote: In all spectra, the stationary component (in red) shows energy levels one order of magnitude larger than the vertically propagating components

steps.action: The authors contrast the cases. Ice-covered months without eddies show a narrow peak near 12 hr, ice-free months with eddies a broadened band, and the convective March 2018 month low energy; they attribute the broadening to eddy vorticity.
steps.quote: The other spectra show distinct characteristics according to the absence or presence of mesoscale activity (mainly anticyclonic).

steps.action: The authors compute the linear-theory criticality parameter for 2K1 and K1 at the mooring slope with two N2 values: near-critical or critical for 2K1 (0.65, 1.45), subcritical for K1 (0.1).
steps.quote: We tentatively computed the critical parameter considering 2K1 and K1 and the slope at the mooring location

steps.action: The authors compare the prediction with the observed semi-diurnal dominance in shear, noting agreement with Wang et al. (2022), and that 2K1 waves propagate freely while M2 waves dissipate locally.
steps.quote: linear theory predicts possible generation of internal waves at the semi-diurnal period at the mooring location

steps.action: The authors set aside internal solitary waves (lee-wave mechanism) as the local source, given the gentle slope and the absence of SAR signals in the region.
steps.quote: Solitary Waves are not expected at the mooring location since the slope is relatively gentle

steps.action: The authors propose that the stationary waves result from interaction of freely propagating 2K1 internal waves generated on both slopes of the narrow plateau, and state that further moorings are needed to test this.
steps.quote: interactions of freely propagating internal waves at period 2K1 (11.97 hr) generated and propagated from both eastern and western slopes

steps.action: The authors conclude that the twin simulations confirm Padman's residual anticyclonic circulation driven mainly by diurnal tides. They keep the 2K1 origin of the stationary shears as probable, pending further observations.
steps.quote: thus confirming Padman et al. (1992)'s hypothesis

tree.answer: Strong high-frequency (tidal, harmonic, near-inertial) velocity and shear variability in the Yermak Pass
Velocities measured directly; residual currents and wave components inferred via models and shear decomposition
Characterize tides and tidal residuals; interpret shear signals as internal waves
Tidal rectification versus no-tide flow; wind-forced NIW, lee/solitary waves and tidally generated 2K1 harmonics; eddy trapping
Criticality parameter separates 2K1 (critical) from K1 (subcritical); eddy vorticity predicts frequency broadening
Conditions found: six months with low mooring motion chosen across ice and eddy regimes; tides set on or off in model twins

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: Yes, the six cases repeat the stationary-shear dominance under varied ice and eddy conditions
Stationary dominance holds in all six cases; simulated residual means stable across averaging periods; criticality similar for two N2 values
Residual anticyclonic circulation kept, said to confirm Padman; stationary-wave mechanism left as a hypothesis

end.claim: Diurnal tides force an anticyclonic residual circulation around the Yermak Plateau that helps Atlantic Water penetrate into the Arctic, so tides must be considered in low-frequency AW inflow studies.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the 1/36° twin simulations with and without tides, there would be no residual-circulation field and no claim of confirming Padman's hypothesis.

gates.evidence: The mooring data were collected earlier for a low-frequency study and reused here. The residual-tide hypothesis directed the choice of tide/no-tide twin simulations (p. 4), which the authors examined rather than designed. The twin simulations could have shown no residual, but they are not contemporaneous, are validated only 'not shown' (p. 9), and are called exploratory. The stationary-wave mechanism is proposed and not tested (p. 15). Nothing is reported as fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: Rotary and two-dimensional wavenumber-frequency spectral analysis of velocity and shear

limits: No peer-review file or earlier version supplied; the acknowledgments mention two reviewers and an editor, but no review sequence could be coded. Supporting Information S1 (tidal tables, 2D shear spectra, Text S2 and S4) was not supplied, so supplementary checks are coded from main-text mentions only. The twin simulations are 3 months long (2013), not contemporaneous with the mooring, have no data assimilation, and their tide validation is 'not shown'. The paper calls this an 'exploratory comparison' yet concludes it 'confirms' Padman; the coder grades it best_explanation (inference). The relation of the selection rule to findings is not reported beyond the pressure criterion. Stratification profiles were not observed, which the authors say restrained the analysis; the criticality computation uses only two N2 values, one taken from another study at 1,000 m. Sub-claims and their statuses: tidal constituents at the mooring, with uncertainties, are estimate_with_resolution. Dominance of stationary over propagating shear in six cases is regularity_in_range (2017-2020, one mooring). Frequency broadening by anticyclonic eddies via effective vorticity is best_explanation. Origin of stationary waves from interacting 2K1 waves is an untested hypothesis (none). Composition coded none_fits: the paper joins two loosely coupled threads, a model twin experiment that sets tides on or off and an observational case series under found conditions. No crucial test is shared among rivals, and the analysis starts by mining existing data rather than from capability or exploration until stable.

disagreements.target: Arc5km2018 barotropic inverse tidal model (Erofeeva & Egbert, 2020)
disagreements.support: Harmonic analysis of the mooring data shows the model underestimates O1 and P1 well outside the observational uncertainties, while matching the other major constituents.
disagreements.quote: [...] and P1 constituents are underestimated by a factor 4.5 and 2, respectively

disagreements.target: YPB transport estimates from ocean models without tides (e.g., PSY4)
disagreements.support: The twin simulations give a tidal residual at the mooring opposite to the mean southeastward YPB flow, consistent with Koenig et al. (2017).
disagreements.quote: Thus, the YPB transport derived from a model without tides may [...] .

alternatives_considered.chosen: Six months (3 winter, 3 summer) with small ADCP pressure variations
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Other months with large mooring motion (pressure variations exceeding 10 m)
alternatives_considered.reason: Large pressure variations could contaminate vertical velocity shear estimates

alternatives_considered.chosen: 1/36° twin simulations with and without tides
alternatives_considered.alternatives: PSY4 1/12° operational system, which lacks tides
alternatives_considered.reason: PSY4 lacks tides and is not fully eddy resolving; the model-observation mean difference may be tidal residual

alternatives_considered.chosen: Mean over 9 January to 26 February 2013 at 77 m shown
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Means over 1, 2 and 3 months; other depths

alternatives_considered.chosen: Both N2 values used for the criticality parameter
alternatives_considered.alternatives: N2 = 3.6e-6 (Urbancic et al., 2022, at 1,000 m) versus N2 = 3.7e-7 (model at depth)
alternatives_considered.reason: Stratification unknown; uncertainty in the estimate
